report:
Reviewed the complete claim: (1) item identity is independent of tracked syntax detail; (2) module rebuilding may change CST or absolute location without replacing semantically unchanged symbols; (3) represented definitions have individually owned CST storage, permitting equal siblings to backdate independently. The referenced architectural foundations explain kind-specific symbol identities and rooted Stashed values; they do not require every syntax node to be an erased symbol.

All four ordinary implementation associations are substantive. parse/mod.rs constructs a Parser and dispatches each represented module item through parse_item_list. parse/items.rs allocates a fresh Stash inside each item constructor, packages its rooted data in Stashed, and passes CST separately from absolute_span to the kind-specific symbol constructor. Functions, structs, enums, traits, impls, constants, statics and aliases use their own CST root; uses have separately owned attributes/imports; modules own attribute stashes and recursively parse children; macro definitions separate attribute storage and tracked token strings; macro invocations own their CST stash. LocalFnSym in local_syms/fns.rs makes name/scope/owner identity fields and cst/span tracked fields. LocalModSym in local_syms/mods.rs likewise separates name/edition/parent from tracked body_source/attrs/span; unexpanded_items is the module reparse boundary. Captured definitions for all other represented kinds have the same tracked-detail separation. Absolute locations are kept in tracked spans; parse/util.rs computes item-relative CST positions independently of absolute starts. Stashed::new computes a rooted fingerprint; equality compares that fingerprint, and salsa::Update returns false for equal Stashed values. Therefore a separately reconstructed equal sibling CST can backdate independently of another sibling's CST change. Associated item lowering, captured as additional context, structurally copies each represented associated definition into its own item_stash; its placement is separately resolved against the owner span. Captured macro parse_output invokes the same parser on generated text and its ParseSource, so generated definitions use the same allocation discipline. The conditional identity guarantee does not promise stability when the identity fields themselves change, or distinguish anonymous equal-key occurrences after arbitrary reorderings.

The complete associated test set contains one ordinary test and one explicit TODO. detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys uses a persistent Database per case, forces an interned-symbol-keyed tracked observer, confirms the warm query log is empty, edits the source, forces the observer again, and asserts the edit log does not contain observe_symbol_identity. Captured helper code confirms ObservedSymbol interns the actual erased Symbol and that query logging records Salsa WillExecute events, so reminting an observed symbol would execute a new observer key. The cases cover a function body, struct field type, enum payload, trait method signature, impl method body, alias target, constant/static initializer, module doc attribute, use path, macro definition body and macro invocation input. The added explicit Error rejection prevents parse-error placeholders from silently satisfying the represented-item checks. Exact source-byte inspection confirmed the original module strings already contained valid Rust quote escapes; no fixture quote change or parser fix was made. The Error guard passed and did not reproduce a compiler failure.

modules_parse_detail_firewall is an honest TODO, not executable verification. Its comment explicitly reserves the persistent movement/body-edit/sibling-insertion-and-reorder matrix, per-item fingerprints, and affected/unaffected downstream reexecution, including generated items. This remains a justified test deferral: completing it requires persistent revision scenarios with independent identity, CST-value and query-execution observations (including a generated-item setup). The ordinary observer test proves the identity facet for its 12 cases; it does not prove span movement, sibling CST equality/backdating or generated downstream reexecution. Those obligations remain visibly deferred rather than being inferred from a passing placeholder. There is no N/A evidence and no implementation TODO reclassification.

Validation performed: cargo fmt; cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib detail_edits_preserve_local_symbol_query_keys passed (1 test); cargo build passed with existing warnings. Earlier the same focused ordinary test also passed before the Error guard. After the association and test changes, started a fresh review, inspected its updated fragments, and recaptured the additional implementation/helper dependencies via review read, verifying their current contents. Central delegated post-codegen and Sage sanity reviews are coordinated by root. No production behavior change was needed. All claim aspects are accounted for by inspected implementation, the substantive identity test, and the explicit remaining TODO coverage; no further edits requested for this review.
